newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Solvay to pay $45mln to up stake in Indupa.
newsitem.headline: Solvay to pay $45mln to up stake in Indupa.

text.p: The Argentine unit of Belgium's Solvay SA SA will pay about $45 million for an additional stake in Indupa SA, the petrochemical company it already controls, an Indupa source said Thursday.
"The deal to be closed in coming months will raise Solvay's stake in Indupa to 51.1 percent, in line with its 51.1 percent voting power," the source told Reuters.
Solvay, through its local unit Solvay Quimica Argentina SA, directly and indirectly holds 39.6 percent of Indupa, Agentina's major producer of PVC and caustic soda.

Solvay has a 70 percent in Derivados Petroquimicos, which owns 38 percent of Indupa. The remaining 30 percent of Derivados is owned by U.S. Dow Chemical Co with 21 percent and local oil giant YPF SA with nine percent.
"Solvay is buying that remaining 30 percent of Derivados for about $45 million," the source said.

On Tuesday Indupa announced it will invest $66 million to expand its caustic soda and vinyl chloride monomer, or VCM, the base of polyvinyl chloride, or PVC, capacities to meet growing local and foreign demand.
The investment will be channelled to upgrade its electrolysis and VCM plants in Bahia Blanca, 400 miles (600 kilometers) south of Buenos Aires. Both projects will be operative around December 1998.
The Indupa source said caustic soda output will be raised to 163.000 tonnes a year from the current 95,000 and that of VCM will grow to 210,000 tonnes a year from 160,000.
Indupa produces 76,000 tonnes of PVC a year. It has 500 employees. In 1996 it had revenues of more than $200 million.
